title: Feeder trigger status
description: Retained on <prefix>/status, republished every telemetry.status_interval_s. A flat object of scalars: that is the shape that survives being graphed, alerted on and diffed. It replaces two retained topics the predecessor published separately -- a bare 'online'/'offline' string on /status and a bare integer reset code on /reset. See docs/message_changes.md.

ts.description: Epoch milliseconds, or 0 when the clock has not been set by NTP. Zero rather than a plausible 1970 date: a consumer can drop a zero, but it cannot detect a decades-old timestamp it has already graphed.

firmware.description: The project name the image was built under. OTA refuses an image whose name differs, so this is also what an update has to match.

provisioned.description: False when feeder_id is 0. An unprovisioned device joins the network and answers the console but publishes no measurements.

reset_reason.description: Why the device last restarted. A word rather than the platform's integer code, which needed the vendor header to read.

heap_min.description: The low-water mark since boot. A steadily falling value is a leak; heap_free alone is too noisy to show one.

wifi_bssid.description: The access point associated with, as aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff; empty when not associated. On an SSID served by several access points, a change here between reports is a roam or a reconnect to a different one.

wifi_link_losses.description: Times an established link dropped since boot. Roams are not counted.

wifi_roams.description: BSS transitions since boot: moves to another access point on the same SSID, steered by the network.

wifi_disconnect_reason.description: ESP-IDF wifi_err_reason_t of the most recent disconnect, including failed connection attempts; 0 when there has been none. Common: 200 beacon timeout, 201 no AP found, 15 4-way handshake timeout, 8 this station left, 4 inactivity, 12 BSS transition.

wifi_disconnect_rssi.description: dBm at the most recent disconnect; 0 when there has been none

wifi_disconnect_ago_s.description: Seconds since the most recent disconnect; -1 when there has been none

sensor_ok.description: The most recent conversion attempt succeeded

initialized.description: The startup baseline has been acquired. No trigger can be asserted before this.

weight_g.description: The most recent sample, absolute feeder mass

delta_g.description: abs(baseline - weight) for the most recent sample

counts_per_gram.description: The calibration factor in force. May be negative for a cell wired in the opposite polarity.

calibration_source.description: 'measured' means a tare or factor from NVS is in force; 'configured' means the config.json defaults are.

sample_rate_hz.description: loadcell.rate_sps divided by loadcell.average_samples. Consumers reconstructing per-sample times from a raw_batch duration should prefer the duration; this is what the device believes it is doing.

rebaselines.description: How many times the baseline was re-acquired after a long excursion. A rising count means the feeder is being refilled, knocked, or drifting.

settled_ago_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last settled sample; -1 before the baseline is acquired. Approaching trigger.rebaseline_after_s means a re-baseline is imminent.

temperature_c.description: Last SHT4x reading; 0 when sht4x is not 'ok'

power_healthy.description: The INA237's trim memory checksum is good and no arithmetic overflow occurred. It deliberately says nothing about whether the part has been reset: the driver writes only SHUNT_CAL, and the value it writes is that register's own reset value, so a reset part comes back configured exactly as this firmware configured it.

part_state.description: 'not-tried' means the bus the part is on was disabled in the board configuration
